name: bounded-self-nesting
body:
A section declaration may accept its own template, directly or through a cycle, when a declaration on the cycle carries `max_depth: N` — a positive integer (for a declaration that accepts its own template, max_depth sits on that declaration). The loader walks the declaration graph bounded by max_depth, so a self-referencing or cyclic declared-section acceptance is valid: content may nest the repeated template under itself up to N self-nested levels, and the walk stops at the bound instead of reporting a cycle. The loader walks each bounded cycle to its full max_depth, and the heading-level chain that walk produces — the cycle's composition prefix plus one heading per bounded level — is measured against the six-heading-level bound (requirements.constraint.section-depth-limit): a declared `max_depth` whose full walk would exceed six heading levels is refused at load as a templates error, the depth-limit error naming the chain and the `max_depth` that produces it, so every declared `max_depth` is reachable in content. A reference cycle whose declarations carry no max_depth is a templates error, the chain error of requirements.constraint.section-cycle-error-chain; bounded self-nesting is the one accepted declared-section cycle. `max_depth` is a positive integer on a section declaration; a value that is not a positive integer is a templates error naming the offending `template.yaml`.

The authored Markdown syntax is unchanged: a self-nested instance is a heading one level deeper than its parent, naming the declaring section slot (slide-sections), so nesting depth is heading depth and no new author-facing syntax exists. Depth is enforced when the content is parsed, at every level: an instance of the repeated template whose self-nesting depth would exceed the declaration's max_depth is a slide error path-qualified to the offending slide file with its containment chain (error-reporting, nested-section-validation), carrying the message `section ""loop"": nesting deeper than max_depth 1`.

Each nested instance carries the ordinary reserved section context (template-context, item-context). `.item.depth` is the instance's self-nesting depth: the number of enclosing instances whose resolved template is the same template — 0 at the outermost instance of that template in the containment chain and +1 at each self-nested level. `.item.parent` is the enclosing instance at every level; `.item.section` is the declared section name at that level (for example `events` at the top and `loop` nested); `.item.index` and `.item.count` are the instance's real position within its group of siblings at each level. `max_depth: N` bounds `.item.depth` at N, so an instance whose `.item.depth` would exceed N is the depth error above while an instance at depth N is accepted.

A `section` helper call is a composition reference but not a section declaration, so it carries no max_depth and a helper-closed cycle is a templates error (section-helper-load-checks); bounded self-nesting widens the declared-section acceptance graph only and leaves section-helper pass-through rendering unchanged.

AC: a template that declares a `loop` section accepting itself with `max_depth: 1` loads with no cycle error, and a slide nesting `# events` › `## loop` parses and renders, the nested `loop` instance reading `.item.depth` 1, its `.item.parent` the enclosing `events` instance, its `.item.section` `loop`, and its `.item.index`/`.item.count` its real position among its `loop` siblings; a `### loop` nested under a `## loop` (self-nesting depth 2) is a slide error carrying the message `section ""loop"": nesting deeper than max_depth 1`; the same self-accepting declaration without `max_depth` is refused at load with the chain error `section template reference cycle: sections/loop → sections/loop`; a `max_depth` that is not a positive integer is a templates error naming the `template.yaml`; a slide → `events` → `loop` chain whose `loop` declaration carries `max_depth: 5` — five `loop` headings under the `events` and slide headings, seven heading levels in all — is refused at load with the depth-limit templates error naming the chain and `max_depth: 5`, because every declared `max_depth` is walked to its full depth; one template that declares `loop` accepting itself with `max_depth: 1` replaces the near-identical timeline-event and loop-event templates, rendering a top `events` instance holding `loop` children that hold no further `loop` children; the authored Markdown syntax is unchanged; a `section`-helper cycle is refused at load.
